This petition is filed by the petitioner under Section 166 of M.V.Act, 1989 claiming compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- in respect of injuries sustained by him in the Road Traffic Accident.

sentences.text: In the petition it is stated that on 26.08.2023 at about 10.00 am, petitioner was proceeding in his m o t o r c y c l e b e a r i n g R e g .
N o . K A - 0 2 - K R - 4 3 1 7 o n B a n g a l o r e - M y s o r e r o a d n e a r Channapattana-Maddur service road at Chakkere cross by observing traffic rules.

At that time, all of a sudden one Car bearing No.KA-04-KR-4137 ( as per FIR car No. is shown as KA- 04-AA-3216)
driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner came from opposite direction and dashed to the petitioner's vehicle and caused accident, due to which, petitioner fell down from the bike and sustained fracture of right distal radius and injuries to face and all over the body.
Immediately petitioner was shifted to Gangappa hospital wherein he took treatment as inpatient for 3 days.
Surgery was conducted and implants were fixed to the petitioner.
He was discharged from the hospital with an advice for follow up treatment and bed rest for 3 months.
He has spent Rs.1,50,000/-towards medical, conveyance, nourishment and other incidental charges.
Prior to the date of accident, he was hale and healthy and working as Delivery Boy at Kanthi Sweets, Bengaluru and earning Rs.25,000/- per (SCCH-12) 3 MVC.No.5766/2023 month.
Now he is suffering from disability and has lost future income and earning capacity.
The accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of offending vehicle.
The Channapattana Traffic police have registered a case in Crime No.163/2023 against the said driver for the offence p/u/s 279, 337 of IPC.
Therefore respondent no.1 insurance company and respondent no.2 owner of the car are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to petitioner.
On all these grounds he prayed to allow the petition and award compensation along with interest and costs in the above case.
3. On issuance of notice, respondent no.2 is served.
He remained absent on the date of hearing and hence, he is placed exparte.
Respondent No.1 insurance company appeared through its counsel and has filed written statement contending that petition is not maintainable either in law or on facts.
It has denied the issuance of policy in favour of 2 nd respondent in respect of Car bearing No.KA-04-AA-3216 and its validity since it is not been confirmed by the concerned policy issuing office.

If the owner of the vehicle were to produce the original policy before this court and their liability if any, is subject to terms and conditions of policy and subject to compliance of 64VB of Insurance Act.
It disputed the compliance of Sec.134(c) and 158(6) of IMV Act.
Negligence on part of car driver is denied.
That the the 2nd respondent has willfully entrusted his vehicle to a person who did not possess valid and effective driving license to drive the vehicle as on the date of accident.
As such, policy (SCCH-12) 4 MVC.No.5766/2023 conditions are violated.
In addition to that petitioner was riding his motor cycle without having D.L insurance and not wearing helmet and has violated the rules and regulations of Motor Vehicle Rules.
Medical treatment and expenses alleged are denied.
Age, occupation and income of the petitioner are denied.
The amount claimed by the petitioner is highly exorbitant without any legal basis.
Loss of earning capacity and financial loss of the petitioner are denied.
On all these grounds he prayed to dismiss the petition.

4. On the basis of above pleadings, I have framed the following:-

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 1. Whether the petitioner proves that on 26.08.2023 at about 10.00 am petitioner was riding motor cycle bearing reg.No.KA- 02-KR-4317 near Channapatna-Maddur service road, Chakkere cross, by observing traffic rules and one car bearing reg.No.KA- 04-KR-4137 driven by its driver in rash and negligent manner and dashed to the aforesaid two wheeler and caused accident due to which petitioner sustained grievous injuries as alleged?
2. Whether the petitioner proves his age, occupation, income and permanent disability if any?
3. Whether the petitioner is entitled for the compensation?
If so by whom and what is the quantum?
4 . What Order or Award?
5. To prove his case, petitioner is examined as P.W.1.
Ex.P.1 to P.15 documents are marked on his behalf.
Doctor by name (SCCH-12) 5 MVC.No.5766/2023 S.A.Somashekara -Orthopedic surgeon at Victoria hospital is examined as P.W.2 and through him Ex.P.16 and 17 documents are marked.
On respondent side no evidence is led.

6. On taking into consideration the oral and documentary evidence placed before this Tribunal and on hearing arguments, my answers to the above issues as under:
 Issue No.1: In the Affirmative,
 Issue No.2: Partly in the Affirmative  Issue No.3: Partly in the Affirmative  Issue No.4: As per final order, for the following;
 REASONS 7. ISSUE NO.1 : As per the petition averments accident took place on 26.08.2023 at about 10.00 am when petitioner was riding two wheeler on Channapatna-Maddur Service road.
To prove this fact and injuries sustained by him, petitioner filed chief examination affidavit and got examined as P.W.1.
He has produced FIR, first information, rough sketch, spot panchanama, vehicle seizure mahazar, IMV report, final report, wound certificate and discharge summary at Ex.P.1 to 9.

They show that one Dwarakesh has given information to Channapatna police on the same day of the accident stating that he received phone call stating his son sustained injury in the accident and he should visit the hospital.

That he went to the Gangappa hospital and found that his son/ petitioner herein got injured and got to know from the petitioner that by rash and negligent driving of the car bearing No.KA-04-AA-3216 which came from opposite direction hit the petitioners bike, due (SCCH-12) 6 MVC.No.5766/2023 to which he sustained injuries.

On the basis of that information Channapatna police registered Crime No.163/2023 against the car driver for the offence p/u/s 279,
337 of IPC and after investigation they filed charge sheet against him for the offence p/u/s 279, 338 of IPC.

sentences.text: As per the wound certificate petitioner sustained RTA on 26.09.2023 and sustained grievous injury of fracture right distal radius.
As per the spot panchanama extent of the road is not mentioned and there is one hotel nearby the spot of accident.
There is entry road of NH-275 at the spot of accident.
The rough sketch produced at Ex.P.4 shows that accident took place on Channapatna to Maddur service road on the left side.
There is also Madduru to Channapatna service road at the same highway.
Therefore, on both sides of the main road there are service roads.

9. As per the final report petitioner was riding on Channapatna-Maddur service road on the left side and the car came from the Maddur side towards Channapatna in high speed in rash and negligent manner.

If the same is considered though there was another service road to go to Madduru side to Channapatna side, car driver came to the service road from Channapatna to Maddur side and hit the bike which was coming on the correct side of the road.
As per the IMV report right side of the car got damaged and bike got severely damaged.
This clearly shows the gravity of the speed at which the car was moving and negligence on part of car driver.
The driver and owner of car have not questioned the FIR and any (SCCH-12) 7 MVC.No.5766/2023 other police documents filed against driver and in respect of involvement of the car.
Though 1st respondent contended that petitioner himself was negligent, not led any evidence to prove the said fact.
In cross examination he suggested the same to P.W.1 which is denied by P.W.1.
Therefore, in the absence of any evidence 1st respondent has failed to prove any negligence on part of the petitioner in riding the bike.

In that view of the matter I am of the opinion that, petitioner by oral and documentary evidence has proved that the driver of the car was rash and negligent in driving the same and caused accident to petitioner.
Accordingly, this issue is answered in the Affirmative.
10. ISSUE NO.2 :
In respect of age, petitioner produced his aadhaar card at Ex.P.14 which shows that he was born on 12.07.2003.
The same is found in his D.L produced at Ex.P.15 also.
Accident took place on 26.08.2023.
He was aged 20 years at the time of accident.
Therefore, the age of the petitioner is considered as 20 years at the time of accident.

11. In respect of occupation it is stated that, petitioner was a Delivery Boy working at Kanthi Sweets,
Bengaluru and was earning Rs.25,000/- per month.
To prove his earnings petitioner has not produced any document.
Hence, notional income has to be considered Rs.15,000/- per month and same is considered as his monthly income.
12. In respect of permanent disability a doctor by name S.A.Somashekar- Orthopaedic Surgeon at Victoria hospital, is examined as P.W.2.
In his chief examination he stated that (SCCH-12) 8 MVC.No.5766/2023 petitioner has sustained Right distal radius fracture and closed displaced intra articular volar barton's fracture.
Surgery was conducted in the form of ORIF with Buttress plate under Brachial Block on 27.08.2023.

He has examined the petitioner recently on 23.12.2024 and found that the petition has diffuse swelling of right wrist and surgical scars are present and his recent X-ray shows united fracture with implant in situ.
P.W.2 has assessed physical disability of 28% of left upper limb and 14% of whole body.
13. In the cross examination the assessment made by the doctor is disputed.
It is elicited that no other documents are perused by the doctor except wound certificate and discharge summary.

There Prajwal M D vs Reliance Gen Ins Co Ltd on 8 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/108287111/
4 are implants in the place of surgery and fracture is united.

sentences.text: There are no other complications in the injury.
As per the evidence of doctor petitioner has whole body disability of 14%.
Considering the occupation of the petitioner as Delivery Boy, the disability in left lower limb will affect his income.
Accordingly functional disability affecting the income of the petitioner is held by this tribunal as 10%.
Accordingly, I answer this issue Partly in the Affirmative.
14. ISSUE NO.3 :
In view of above reasons, injuries sustained by petitioner are due to the accident caused by the driver of the car bearing No.KA-04-AA-3216.
There is nexus between the injuries sustained by the petitioner and the accident.
Hence, he is entitled to compensation at the hands of respondents.

1 st respondent has not given evidence denying the issuance of policy therefore 1st respondent is liable to indemnify the insured (SCCH-12) 9 MVC.No.5766/2023 and liable to pay compensation to petitioner.

The quantum of compensation is determined as under:
(i) Medical expenses:
The petitioner has produced medical bills at Ex.P10.
Totally he has paid amount of Rs.99,342/- as per Ex.P.10 medical bills.
The said payment of bill is due to the accident caused to him.
They are subsequent to the date of accident.
Though they are disputed, no satisfactory material is placed to disbelieve the bills.
They are supported by prescriptions of the doctor.
Therefore, petitioner is entitled for medical expenses of Rs.99,342/-.
(ii) Food and nourishment:
The petitioner was admitted in Gangappa Multispeciality hospital from 26.08.2023 and discharge on 29.08.2023 and has produced discharge summary at Ex.P.9.
He was in hospital for 04 days.
Accident took place in the year 2023.
Since he was in hospital, food and nourishment charges will have to be awarded.
Considering the cost of living, and food, nourishment charges if per day Rs.500/- is awarded it will meet the ends of justice.
Hence for food and nourishment Rs.500/- x 04 days = Rs.2,000/-is awarded.
(iii) Attendant charges:
For a period of inpatient for 04 days someone should have looked after petitioner in the hospital.
Even if his family member has taken care of him in the said period, that family member's income for those days is lost.
Hence per day if Rs.500/- is awarded as attendant charges in 2023, it will meet the ends of justice.
Hence for attendant charges Rs.500/- x 04 days =Rs.2,000/-is awarded.
(SCCH-12) 10 MVC.No.5766/2023 (iv) Loss of income during laid up period:
As per the finding to issue No.2, the income of the petitioner per month is Rs.15,000/-.
He suffered grievous injuries.
He was inpatient for 04 days and he was advised to take rest.
Minimum 2 months is required to recover from such grievous injury.

Therefore, laid up period of petitioner is considered as total 2 months including in patient period and loss of income during laid up period is Rs.15,000/-x 2= Rs. 30,000/- He is entitled to Rs.30,000/- as loss of income during laid up period.
Prajwal

5 (v) Conveyance charges:

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is stated that petitioner took treatment at Gowdappa multispeciality hospital.
He has spent money for conveyance for the purpose of treatment.
Hence, conveyance charges of Rs.3,000/- is awarded.
(vi) Loss of future income due to Disability :
As per the findings given to issue no.2, there is functional disability of 10%.
Therefore, loss of future income due to disability is to be calculated as income per month Rs.15,000 X 12 months X 10% disability X appropriate multiplier to the age group of 15-25 is 18.
Hence, in the opinion of this court, petitioner is entitled for a sum of Rs.3,24,000/- towards loss of future income due to disability.

(vii) For Future medical expenses: P.W.2 doctor who has assessed the disability of the petitioner has stated that petitioner needs to removal the implants which may require Rs.40,000/- but no estimation is produced.

In view of necessity of removal of implants for well being of the petitioner in the (SCCH-12) 11 MVC.No.5766/2023 opinion of this court amount of Rs.25,000/- shall be awarded for future medical treatment.
Accordingly, Rs.25,000/- is awarded under this head.
(viii) For Pain and sufferings:
The petitioner has sustained grievous injuries as per the wound certificate produced by him.
The records show that he underwent operation.
He was in hospital for 04 days and he underwent surgery therefore, he sustained pain and sufferings.
For pain and suffering the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.30,000/- .
(ix) Physical discomfort and loss of amenities of life :

As per the evidence of treated doctor,
petitioner complained about difficulty in lifting overhead objects remove and placing at the same place, eating Indian style, combing and plaiting, putting on shirt button ablution Indian style.
He suffers discomfort.
Meaning, he cannot lead the normal life as he used to live before the accident.
Certainly accident has caused physical discomfort and come in the way of normal enjoyment of life.
Hence in the opinion of this court, petitioner is entitled to compensation under the head of physical discomfort and loss of amenities of life.

Under the said head he is entitled for Rs.40,000/-
(x) Loss of future prospect:
As per the evidence of assessed doctor, petitioner complained about pain and restriction in movement but there is no specific evidence regarding future prospects loss of the petitioner.
Hence, no compensation is awarded under this head.

Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for compensation as follows:-

Therefore, I hold that the petitioner is entitled for a total compensation of Rs.5,55,342/- in respect of injuries sustained by him in the Road traffic accident.
Accordingly, I answer this Issue "Partly in Affirmative".
15. ISSUE NO.4:-

In view of above reasons, I proceed to pass following :
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioner u/Sec.166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with costs.

It is held that, petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.5,55,342/- with interest @ 6% pa on the amount of Rs.
5,30,342/- from the date of petition till the date of payment.
(Future medical expenses of Rs. 25,000/- will not carry interest)
The respondent no.1 insurance company is liable to indemnify the insured and directed to deposit the aforesaid compensation amount with interest within 2 months from the date of this order.

On such deposit petitioner is entitled to have release of 50% compensation and remaining 50% shall be kept in F.D in the name of petitioner in any nationalized bank of his choice with a liberty to draw periodical interest.
The Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Award be drawn accordingly.

ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioner u/Sec.166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with costs.

It is held that, petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.5,55,342/- with interest @ 6% pa on the amount of Rs.
5,30,342/- from the date of petition till the date of payment.
(Future medical expenses of Rs. 25,000/- will not carry interest)
The respondent no.1 insurance company is liable to indemnify the insured and directed to deposit the aforesaid compensation amount with interest within 2 months from the date of this order.

On such deposit petitioner is entitled to have release of 50% compensation and remaining 50% shall be kept in F.D in the name of petitioner in any nationalized bank of his choice with a liberty to draw periodical interest.
The Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
